doc_verification.detail: Reachability: WebFetch to api.qdrant.tech returned domain_blocked; fallback fetch via web reader succeeded and returned the full page (title 'Create a collection | Qdrant | API Reference') - PASS with tool-path disclosure. Version: URL is the versioned /v-1-18-x/ api-reference, matching target v1.18.0 on major.minor - PASS. Content: the page's own words document shard_number as 'uint or null Optional ... For auto sharding: Number of shards in collection. - Default is 1 for standalone, otherwise equal to the number of nodes - Minimum is 1' (and the custom-sharding variant likewise 'Minimum is 1') with NO documented maximum - the constraint's factual premise is verbatim-consistent; the graceful-handling obligation itself is the contract's own declared inferred tier, and no source_verified flag contradicts it. Endpoint: endpoint_registry entry 'collections+create' PUT with the same source_url and doc_quote 'Successful operation returns 200 with CollectionOperationResponse...' matches the page and the request actually sent - PASS.

http_semantics.note: No HTTP response of any class was returned - the server closed the connection mid-request (RemoteDisconnected) because the process died; strictly worse than 2xx-masking. The input was decidable (spec-legal per the documented uint/min-1/no-max contract), so the graceful options were 200-completed, 4xx-rejected, or descriptive-5xx; none occurred.

contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: inferred: any spec-legal shard_number (>= 1, no documented max) must be completed, rejected with an error, or fail with a documented service error - never crash the service
contract_grounding.note: violates-declaration self-check: the claim's phenomenon is service death on a spec-legal value, and 4294967295 lies inside the quote's constraint domain (>= 1, no documented max - doc-verified verbatim), so violates=true is sound with no constraint-citation change. None of the three allowed dispositions occurred: not completed (no 200), not rejected (no 4xx), no documented service error (no response at all; process death confirmed by /healthz dead ~12 min).

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: PUT /collections/{name} -> CreateCollection schema struct, validation = #[validate(range(min = 1))] ONLY (lib/api/build.rs:127; the 422 for shard_number=0 seen in boundary_013 is this attribute rendering through validation.rs) -> TableOfContent::perform_collection_meta_op (collection_meta_ops.rs:57-61: standalone, number_of_peers=1, user shard_number passed through unchanged) -> CollectionShardDistribution::all_local materializes an AHashMap over (0..4294967295), each entry carrying a heap-allocated HashSet (collection_shard_distribution.rs:16-18) -> create_collection.rs:135 NonZeroU32 zero-check only -> Collection::new loops one ShardReplicaSet::build per entry (collection/mod.rs:130). At uint32 max the distribution map alone is on the order of hundreds of GB before a single shard exists; the process dies mid-request (RemoteDisconnected, /healthz 000 ~12 min until external restart). No upper-bound constant or check exists anywhere in lib/ (grep MAX_SHARD/max_shard/too many shards: zero validation hits), and no comment/docstring declares the absence intentional; contrast VectorParams.size which carries an explicit max=65536 in the same registry, and the boundary_013 matrix which shows feasible extremes (1000, 100000) timing out with healthz alive - only uint32 max is fatal.

mundane_explanation.surviving: container memory ceiling is the proximate kill mechanism for the allocation storm - on hypothetically unbounded hardware uint32-max might degrade from 'death' to an unresolvable hang, but that alternative is itself a forbidden outcome under the same assertion (neither completed, rejected, nor a documented error), so the violation survives at any memory size
